<!-- name: Off the Grid -->
<!-- board: LoRa listening on the watches | Privacy Mode for filming | Charge Mode and a BOOT button that does things -->
**Off the Grid.** Squachy grew a third ear. WiFi and Bluetooth were never the only things in the air: out past the routers there are whole radio networks, Meshtastic and MeshCore, run by people with antennas on their roofs and strong opinions about firmware. The T-Watch has had a LoRa radio sitting inside it this whole time, doing nothing. It listens now. He never talks back, he just eavesdrops politely, which is very on brand.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.26.0/docs/off-the-grid.gif" width="480" alt="Squachy on his main screen, then the LOG as it normally looks, then the same LOG with Privacy Mode on: addresses end in XX and names are cut to three letters and stars. Then an alert card with Privacy Mode on, and the System settings page with the PRIVACY MODE row."></p>

**LoRa on the watches.** Both T-Watch S3 models (plain and Plus) now listen to Meshtastic and MeshCore at once and sort what they hear into two chats, one per network. Public channels read in full: Meshtastic's default LongFast channel, and MeshCore's Public and hashtag channels. Private traffic stays private, because he hasn't got the keys and isn't that kind of cryptid. When something new arrives you get a pink LORA NEW pill on the main screen (tap it) and one polite buzz. WATCH SETTINGS > LORA picks BOTH, MESHTASTIC, MESHCORE or OFF, and the band follows your time zone, 915 in the Americas and 868 elsewhere. Huge thanks to DH5DAX, whose CrowPanel work this is built from: the radio driver and every decoder are theirs. On the bench it caught 26 of 26 test messages across both networks. In the wild it has heard exactly one stranger so far, from very far away. Go find it some company.

**Privacy Mode.** For anyone who films this thing, which now includes the management. SETTINGS > SYSTEM > PRIVACY MODE hides the half of every address that identifies the device (the maker half stays) and cuts every device and network name to three letters and stars. So the neighbour's doorbell is still a RING, still that loud, still that close, and no longer has anybody's name on it. It covers alerts, the log, the scan lists, the WiFi screens and the LoRa chats. It only changes what's on screen: the saved log and the WiGLE file keep the real thing.

**The watch stops waking up for every AirTag.** A day on a wrist turned out to be fifty AirTags an hour in traffic, and every one of them lit the screen. WATCH SETTINGS > TAGS + RINGS is now LOG ONLY by default: AirTags, Tiles, Samsung and Google tags and Ring cameras are still logged, but they don't wake the watch or buzz. Flock cameras, drones, hackers and anything on your watch list still do. Flip it back to ALERT if you liked the attention. Also on the watch: the GPS takes a rest when it can't see the sky instead of searching all day indoors, the S3 Plus charges twice as fast, and three tools left over from an old bug hunt (RADIO RESET, STEADY POWER, CLOCK CHECK) have been shown the door.

**Charge Mode, for boards with a battery.** Some CYD boards can't be switched off while they charge, so most of the charger's effort goes into running the board. SETTINGS > CHARGE MODE turns off the radios, the light and the screen so the battery gets nearly all of it. Tap the dark screen to see how long it's been charging, tap again to wake up. And since most of these boards can't report their battery, SETTINGS > SYSTEM > LAST RUN now tells you how long the board ran last time, so you can finally find out what that battery is really worth.

**The BOOT button does something.** On the standard CYD boards, a short press turns the screen off (he keeps listening, and an alert still lights it up), another turns it back on, and holding it for a second starts Charge Mode. It's been sitting there the whole time. Somebody had to give it a job.

**Time zones go both ways.** The time zone row is now ZONE < >. Left side steps back, right side steps forward. Overshooting your zone no longer costs you a lap of the planet.

**The 3.5" stops seeing double.** On the 3.5" board the WiFi password keyboard, the Diary and a few other screens drew one half of themselves twice. Thanks to philchamp51 for the report and rrahmani for the photos and a diagnosis good enough to frame. It's fixed in the code but not yet confirmed on a real 3.5", so if you have one, tell us.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- LoRa listening on the T-Watch S3 and S3 Plus (receive only): Meshtastic and MeshCore, public channels decoded, EU 868 and US 915 band plans picked from the time zone. WATCH SETTINGS > LORA (BOTH / MESHTASTIC / MESHCORE / OFF) and LORA CHATS, one tab per network.
- A LORA NEW pill on the watch's main screen and one buzz per new message (at most one every 30 seconds).
- PRIVACY MODE (SETTINGS > SYSTEM): addresses shown as AA:BB:CC:XX:XX:XX, device and network names cut to three characters. Screen only.
- TAGS + RINGS on the watch (LOG ONLY by default): trackers and Ring cameras are logged without waking the screen or buzzing.
- CHARGE MODE on the CYD boards: radios, status light and screen off while charging.
- LAST RUN (SETTINGS > SYSTEM) on the CYD boards: how long the previous power-up lasted. RUNTIME on the console lists the last eight.
- The BOOT button on the standard CYD boards: short press for screen off and on, hold for Charge Mode.
- Console: LORA (status, NODES, MSGS, REGION AUTO|EU|US), PINS, I2C, CHARGE, RUNTIME.

**Changed**
- The time zone row steps both ways: left half back, right half forward.
- The watch's GPS powers down for five minutes after ten minutes without a fix, then looks again for two.
- The T-Watch S3 Plus charges at 400 mA (the plain watch stays at 200).
- On the watch, Squachy's speech bubbles draw over the GPS bar instead of under it.
- RADIO RESET, STEADY POWER and CLOCK CHECK are gone from WATCH SETTINGS. The automatic radio self-heal stays.

**Fixed**
- 3.5": the WiFi password keyboard, the Diary and other menus drew one half of the screen twice (#25). Not yet confirmed on hardware.
